ledger.note: 1177: the Duchy of Kalisz is created in the partition of the Duchy of Greater Poland. 'The duchy was established in 1177, following the partition of the Duchy of Greater Poland after a rebellion against Mieszko III'; first duke Casimir II the Just (1177-1181); a fiefdom within the Duchy of Poland until 1227. Land is the page's 'Kalisz Land'; its extent is my reading.

region.text: Kalisz Land seized by Mieszko III

ledger.note: 1181: Mieszko III retakes Kalisz. 'In 1181, Mieszko III the Old seized Gniezno and Kalisz, which had belonged to the Seniorate Province.' The Kalisz page ends Casimir II's rule in the same year.

wars.name: Odon's revolt against Mieszko III the Old
wars.outcome: Odon backed the 1177-79 challenge to his father, expelled him from the Greater Polish lands in 1179, and was forced out of Poznań in 1181; Mieszko III seized Gniezno and Kalisz in 1181.
wars.note: No standalone Wikipedia article is cited; the page says Odon 'feared for his inheritance'. Whether Kalisz itself was fought over before 1181 is not stated.

wars.name: Władysław III Spindleshanks against Władysław Odonic for Greater Poland
belligerents: Henry I the Bearded (Duchy of Silesia)

zones.text: the Kalisz division of Greater Poland, held by Odonic

wars.outcome: From 1217 Spindleshanks, reconciled with Leszek I and Henry I the Bearded, expelled his nephew Odonic; after Leszek's death in 1227 Odonic won, taking all of Greater Poland in 1229 while Spindleshanks fled to Silesia.
wars.note: Zone is the Kalisz placeholder shape; the page does not say where the fighting took place.

certainty.note: Neither page describes the duchy's borders, and it was repeatedly joined to and split from Greater Poland; every frontier is approximate.

sources.title: Duchy of Kalisz
sources.note: Identity: established 1177, fiefdom until independence in 1227, ended 1279, capital Kalisz, first and last dukes. Thin: no borders, area or middle rulers.

sources.title: Duchy of Greater Poland
sources.note: Second page: Kalisz's 1181 seizure, 1191-1194 dukes, the infobox division windows 1191-1194, 1207-1229, 1234-1238, 1247-1250, 1253-1257, 1277-1279, and the Spindleshanks-Odonic conflict.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 used. Cliopatria's row (1210-1219, 2,819 km2) covers only ten years of a duchy that the Kalisz page dates 1177-1279; the dossier therefore adds new keyframes for the windows in which the Greater Poland infobox shows Kalisz as a separate division, all drawn with the Cliopatria 1210 outline as a placeholder because no page gives borders or an area. The two pages disagree: the Kalisz page says Kalisz was a fiefdom until 1227 and 'existed in this form until 1279', while the Greater Poland page shows Greater Poland reunited between the divisions (1181-1191, 1194-1207, 1229-1234, 1238-1247, 1250-1253, 1257-1277). The ledger follows the Greater Poland windows, so a renderer should draw Kalisz only in the keyframe windows and as part of duchy-of-greater-poland otherwise; where the windows are dated only by the infobox (1207, 1234, 1238, 1250, 1257, 1277) the events are confidence 2. The Kalisz page names Casimir II the Just as first duke (1177-1181) and Przemysł II as last (1273-1279) and gives no list between, so no ruler strip is written. The Greater Poland page's 1193-1194 Odon and 1191 Mieszko the Younger dukes are in the ledger notes only. Neighbours in the seed (Duchy of Greater Poland, Duchy of Opole 1210-1215, Duchy of Silesia 1210-1219, Duchy of Sandomierz 1216-1219) were not opened for border contacts; no contest events are recorded because neither page names fighting that took or held ground inside Kalisz itself. Kalisz is not a gazetteer place name, so every region is a Cliopatria reference.
